cases.explain: «Прусский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Bending forward in his armchair he said: “Le Roi de Prusse!” and having said this laughed. Everyone turned toward him. “Le Roi de Prusse?” Ippolit said interrogatively, again laughing, and then calmly and seriously sat back in his chair. Anna Pávlovna waited for him to go on, but as he seemed quite decided to say no more she began to tell of how at Potsdam the impious Bonaparte had stolen the sword of Frederick the Great.

cases.sentence: — Voyons à qui en avez vous avec votre Roi de Prusse?[437] — Ну, что ж ___?
cases.explain: «прусский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Anna Pávlovna frowned. Mortemart, Ippolit’s friend, addressed him firmly.

cases.sentence: Мы воюем за ___, а не за прусского короля.
cases.explain: «добрые начала» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Your joke is too bad, it’s witty but unjust,” said Anna Pávlovna, shaking her little shriveled finger at him. “We are not fighting pour le Roi de Prusse, but for right principles. Oh, that wicked Prince Hippolyte!” she said.

cases.sentence: Разговор не утихал ___, обращаясь преимущественно около политических новостей.
cases.explain: «целый вечер» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The conversation did not flag all evening and turned chiefly on the political news. It became particularly animated toward the end of the evening when the rewards bestowed by the Emperor were mentioned.

cases.sentence: — Ведь получил же в прошлом году NN табакерку с портретом, — говорил l’homme à l’esprit profond,[441] человек ___, — почему же SS не может получить той же награды?
cases.explain: «глубокого ума» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “You know N—— N—— received a snuffbox with the portrait last year?” said “the man of profound intellect.” “Why shouldn’t S—— S—— get the same distinction?”

cases.sentence: — Пари. Le grand cordon, c’est différent...[445] — Лента — ___...
cases.explain: «другое дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Will you bet? The ribbon of the order is a different matter. …”

cases.sentence: Казалось, что в этот вечер из каких-то слов, сказанных Борисом о ___, Элен вдруг открыла необходимость видеть его.
cases.explain: «прусском войске» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: “It is of great importance to me,” she said, turning with a smile toward Anna Pávlovna, and Anna Pávlovna, with the same sad smile with which she spoke of her exalted patroness, supported Elèn’s wish. It seemed as if from some words Borís had spoken that evening about the Prussian army, Elèn had suddenly found it necessary to see him. She seemed to promise to explain that necessity to him when he came on Tuesday.

cases.sentence: Приехав во вторник вечером в ___ Элен, Борис не получил ясного объяснения, для чего было ему необходимо приехать.
cases.explain: «великолепный салон» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: But on Tuesday evening, having come to Elèn’s splendid salon, Borís received no clear explanation of why it had been necessary for him to come. There were other guests and the countess talked little to him, and only as he kissed her hand on taking leave said unexpectedly and in a whisper, with a strangely unsmiling face: “Come to dinner tomorrow … in the evening. You must come. … Come!”

cases.sentence: Были другие гости, графиня мало говорила с ним, и только прощаясь, когда он целовал ее руку, она с ___ улыбки, неожиданно, шопотом, сказала ему:
cases.explain: «странным отсутствием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: But on Tuesday evening, having come to Elèn’s splendid salon, Borís received no clear explanation of why it had been necessary for him to come. There were other guests and the countess talked little to him, and only as he kissed her hand on taking leave said unexpectedly and in a whisper, with a strangely unsmiling face: “Come to dinner tomorrow … in the evening. You must come. … Come!”

cases.sentence: В этот свой приезд в Петербург Борис сделался ___ в доме графини Безуховой.
cases.explain: «близким человеком» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: During that stay in Petersburg, Borís became an intimate in the countess’ house.
